sections.h2: Who deals with property tax in Calhoun County?
sections.html:
Three layers share the work: a city or township assessor, a local board of review, and the County Treasurer in Marshall. The treasurer's office, in the County Building at 315 West Green Street, collects real estate taxes that go delinquent, balances the books for the county's 28 townships, cities and villages, and manages reversion of unpaid parcels through title searches, property visits, court hearings, foreclosure and auction. It also issues deed certifications and helps run the Calhoun County Land Bank.

  • Delinquent taxes, hardship extensions, deed certification: 269-781-0807.
  • Homestead and taxable value changes: 269-781-0808.
  • Land bank: 269-781-0777.
  • Open Monday to Thursday, 8 a.m. to 5 p.m., and Friday until noon.

Valuation questions on a particular parcel start with the city or township assessor. For the millage on your own bill, ask the treasurer or the local unit that mails it.

sections.h2: How does Michigan set a Calhoun County home's taxable value?
sections.html:
Assessments run at 50% of true cash value. The figure the millage multiplies is taxable value, which may climb each year by no more than the smaller of 5% or inflation and never past state equalized value, per MCL 211.27a. When ownership transfers, the next year's taxable value snaps back to state equalized value.

That snap-back is the part sellers should flag to buyers. A house held down by years of capped increases can produce a noticeably bigger bill for its new owner. As a yardstick, Calhoun County's Census median owner-occupied value is $162,800, and half of that, about $81,400, is what state equalized value would be at the 50% ratio for a house valued at the median.

A buyer with questions about the post-sale bill can call the treasurer's taxable value line, 269-781-0808.

sections.h2: What are the Calhoun County property tax dates?
sections.html:
The calendar comes from state law and repeats every year, so it holds for any Calhoun County parcel.

Annual Michigan tax milestones affecting Calhoun County owners, with statute
StepRuleSource
Board of reviewOpens the second Monday in March; at least 12 hours of hearings that weekMCL 211.30
Principal residence exemptionAffidavit due June 1 to catch the summer bill, November 1 for the winter billMCL 211.7cc
Summer taxBecomes a lien and is due July 1; interest starts after September 14MCL 211.44a
Tax Tribunal, residentialPetition due July 31 of the tax yearMCL 205.735a
Winter fee windowFee of up to 1% when paid before February 15; 3% late charge possible afterwardMCL 211.44
DelinquencySummer taxes still unpaid are returned delinquent March 1MCL 211.44a

Commercial and industrial petitions to the tribunal are due a bit sooner, on May 31.

sections.h2: How can a Calhoun County owner challenge an assessment?
sections.html:
The March board of review is step one. A residential owner has to protest there before the Michigan Tax Tribunal will hear the case, and the board owes a written decision, with notice of appeal rights, by the first Monday in June. A nonresident taxpayer can send the protest and supporting papers by letter instead of appearing.

Still unhappy? File a petition with the tribunal by July 31 for residential and farm property. Postmark, hand delivery or handoff to a designated delivery service by the deadline counts as timely. Serve a copy on the local assessor by certified mail. You can argue your own case or send an attorney or other representative.

A denied principal residence exemption goes first to the July or December board of review. The governing statutes are MCL 211.30 and MCL 205.735a.

sections.h2: What relief exists for Calhoun County owners behind on taxes?
sections.html:
Homeowners working to catch up on forfeited taxes can apply to the treasurer for a financial hardship extension. It pushes the foreclosure deadline back by as much as a year, in return for a payment plan. The extension covers only the time to pay: 1.5% monthly interest, fees and penalties keep accruing, so the debt keeps growing. Apply online, then expect a call to set an appointment. The number is 269-781-0807.

  • Disabled veterans: an honorably discharged Michigan resident who is rated permanently and totally disabled at 100% by the VA, holds a VA certificate for specially adapted housing, or is rated individually unemployable. Surviving spouses can qualify. File the State Tax Commission affidavit with the local assessor each year.
  • Principal residence exemption: file an affidavit with the local tax collecting unit under MCL 211.7cc.
  • Foreclosure auctions: the treasurer's document center carries auction results for 2013 through 2025, which shows what tax-foreclosed parcels brought.

Once a parcel has gone through foreclosure, ask the treasurer how the reversion timeline will run before an auction is scheduled.

sections.h2: How do unpaid taxes affect a Calhoun County house sale?
sections.html:
Taxes follow the property into a sale. The summer bill becomes a lien and falls due July 1, and tax collected after the payable deadline picks up a 4% county fee plus interest at 1% per month, under MCL 211.44. Anything unpaid on March 1 is sent to the county treasurer. The treasurer's website offers pages to look up and pay delinquent taxes, so an owner can see a balance before listing.

For a warranty deed, MCL 211.135 requires the county treasurer to certify that no tax liens or titles are held and that five years of taxes are paid. The Register of Deeds charges $5 for the certification. Arrange payoff through the title company early enough for the certificate to issue before the closing date.

sections.h2: How big is Calhoun County, and who lives there?
sections.html:
Calhoun County covers 706 square miles of land and had an estimated 133,408 residents in 2025, or about 190 per square mile. The count slid 0.7% from the April 2020 base. Battle Creek is the biggest city, and Marshall is the seat.

Age 65 and over describes 20.2% of residents, 14.5% live below the poverty line, and workers average a 20.5 minute commute. Builders took out 120 permits in 2025. Retail sales came to $16,721 per resident in 2022, against $6,832 in neighboring Cass County. Selected monthly owner costs run $1,271 with a mortgage and $545 without.

faqs.q: Which treasurer collects property tax in Calhoun County?
faqs.a: Your city or township treasurer sends the regular bill, and the County Treasurer takes over once taxes are returned delinquent. The county office is at 315 West Green Street in Marshall, phone 269-781-0807.

faqs.q: When does the Calhoun County board of review meet?
faqs.a: It convenes the second Monday in March, or the Tuesday or Wednesday after if the local unit chooses, and meets 12 hours or more that week. Your assessor can give you the local schedule.

faqs.q: What is the filing deadline for the Michigan Tax Tribunal?
faqs.a: For residential, agricultural and timber-cutover real property it is July 31 of the tax year, and for commercial, industrial and developmental property it is May 31. A residential owner must protest to the board of review first.

faqs.q: Can the Calhoun County Treasurer postpone a tax foreclosure?
faqs.a: For homeowners, yes. A financial hardship extension can delay the foreclosure deadline up to one year when a payment plan is in place, though 1.5% monthly interest and fees continue to accrue.

faqs.q: Are Calhoun County property taxes settled at closing?
faqs.a: Normally the title company clears any balance from the sale. Before a warranty deed can be recorded, the county treasurer must certify paid taxes, and the Register of Deeds charges $5 for that.
